baseline: Admit fields whose maximum window cosine is >= 0.70.
candidate: Same absolute floor. Additionally require the maximum minus the unweighted mean cosine of all 32 anchor documents for the query to be >= 0.070. No tuning or rescoring.
encoding: One verified packaged Gemma Q4 worker with below-normal process priority in an isolated evaluator-owned home. Query role for questions and document role for notes and fixed anchors. 96 UTF-16 code units per field window, stride 80. No truncation. Normalize every vector to unit length for cosine. Every input encoded once by role, and the same vectors feed both rules.
ranking: Score only the supplied roster. Sort by descending maximum-window cosine, then by the input pool order. Return up to five admitted field IDs. Baseline/candidate top five committed to an evaluator-private file and publicly hashed before parsing gold. A pilot query has zero or one target candidate ID.
metrics: Top-1 and top-5 hits and MRR@5 on answerables; reciprocal rank zero for missing gold. Any admitted result for a null query is one false accept. Also report null false accepts by direction, pool size and category, and grouped near-topic (missing_number, wrong_entity, absent_attribute) versus chitchat. Chinese-language regression: zh->zh top1/top5, MRR, false accepts, by form/category and pool size. Report all four directions. Counts are descriptive and repeated queries cluster by topic.
gate: Proceed to the next research stage only if top1 and top5 both hold or improve for all answerables and for zh->zh, and total false accepts strictly decrease. Denominators must be identical across the comparison. Otherwise record no support. No post-result threshold change or second blind run.
scope: Independent mathematical admission test for the small-pool synthetic memory supplement. Does not exercise end-to-end retrieval, production injection, authorization, disclosure, integration, latency or full SR2. No model tuning. Do not publish questions, candidate notes, individual predictions or reference labels in the repository.
